aria: Animated recap of the Mavericks' 113 to 109 win at Phoenix: Cooper Flagg's 14-foot turnaround jumper with 23 seconds left that made it 109 to 106, quarter-by-quarter scoring, Flagg's 34 points, 8 assists and 5 steals, the top scorers, how the Mavericks won, and the next game.

figure.label: Cooper Flagg, listed 6-9, 205 lb, No. 32 (RealGM); no sourced wingspan

notes: Box score from StatMuse's game page for the Mavericks' 113–109 win at Phoenix on Nov 27, 2026, the last NBA Cup group game for both teams: all 113 Dallas points and all 109 Phoenix points add up from the player lines, as do the shooting totals (44 of 93, 9 of 30 from three, 16 of 18 FT for Dallas; 41 of 86, 15 of 40, 12 of 14 for Phoenix), rebounds (42–43), assists (31–26) and steals (12–3). The quarter scores (28–25–25–35 to 29–34–32–14) are on StatMuse and Fox Sports. The biggest leads (Dallas 13, Phoenix 21) are on StatMuse; Field Level Media has Phoenix up 21 at 92–71 with 1:49 left in the third. Bench points: Dallas' 49 is the sum of its reserves on StatMuse; Phoenix's 43 is in Field Level Media and adds up on StatMuse. Points in the paint are not shown: no page read had them. Records and ranks are from the site's standings after Friday's games.

Cooper Flagg had 34 points, 7 rebounds, 8 assists, 5 steals and 4 blocks in just under 42 minutes (StatMuse; AP). Dallas won the fourth quarter 35–14 (StatMuse) and has won five straight, finishing 4–0 in NBA Cup group play (AP; Field Level Media) and clinching a home knockout game (Field Level Media). Max Christie scored 14 of his 16 in the fourth and made all four free throws in the last 7 seconds (Field Level Media; StatMuse). Flagg's tip-in with 56 seconds left gave Dallas its first lead since early in the second quarter, 107–106 (StatMuse; Roundtable Sports). Kyrie Irving sat out (left knee injury management) and Caleb Martin left with a left ankle sprain (Field Level Media; Roundtable Sports). Devin Booker: "Just a meltdown" (Arizona Sports). Next: Dallas hosts Boston on Monday; Phoenix plays at Utah on Sunday (AP).

The play of the game is an original illustration of Cooper Flagg's 14-foot turnaround jumper with 23 seconds left that made it 109–106: StatMuse's play-by-play has "C. Flagg makes 14' turnaround jump shot" (no assist) at 0:23 for 107–106 to 109–106; AP: "Flagg made a turnaround jumper for a 109-106 lead" (it gives 22.6 seconds; Field Level Media 23.9), after Booker missed a 16-footer. So the board's Mavericks +1 to +3 is 107–106 to 109–106. The defender and the spot on the floor are not described, so it is drawn with the template's plain pull-up from about 14 feet. The figures are stylized and not traced from footage, and the spacing is not to scale.

The music is an original beat made for this page. No existing recordings or melodies are used. This is an unofficial fan recap, not affiliated with the Dallas Mavericks or the NBA, which is why it carries a plain basketball mark and the team's colors but not the team's logo.

The shooter in the play of the game is drawn to Flagg's listed 6-foot-9 and 205 pounds (RealGM); no wingspan was found in the sources read, so his arms are drawn at his height. He wears the Mavericks' road blue with No. 32 (RealGM) and his proposed look from kit/looks.json. It is an original figure with a featureless face, not a portrait or a trace of footage.
